subject: Draft: Compensation scale decision criteria and geo indexing + offer guardrails
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Mercury Talent <recruiting@mercury-talent.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Compensation scale decision criteria and geo indexing + offer guardrails

Team — attaching a compact draft of the compensation principles and the geo-indexing model (attachments). Goal: land final guardrails this week so Talent can update offer templates and recruiters can start calibrating for active roles. High-level ask: please review the decision criteria and the example market index table, call out anything that would materially change the percentile targets or the uplift caps.

Key points in this draft (high level):
- Source mix: Radford global survey + Levels.fyi anonymized comps + internal offer history for last 12 months.
- Anchor approach: pick a US reference market percentile by level (recommended: 60th for IC Sr/Staff lines, 55th for manager lines) and then apply location multipliers for non-reference markets.
- Geo multipliers: modeled as % of US reference comp (not additive). Preliminary caps for smaller markets so we avoid >+30% uplift.
- Remote hires: default to candidate's primary work location multiplier; exceptions require manager+People Ops signoff.
- Pay mix guidance: show base vs total cash bands (base bands anchored to percentile, variable ranges separate).

Attachments referenced: geo_anchor_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet with example multipliers), comp_scale_principles.docx (draft language).

Requested by EOD Tue 2027-06-08: any objections or quick redlines. I will consolidate and schedule a 30-min sync if needed.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Compensation scale decision criteria and geo indexing + offer guardrails

Thanks Marissa — quick pass below. I like the structure. Two items I think we should tighten before we finalize: 

1) Benchmarks: explicitly call out the vintage and normalization method. Radford Global Tech 2026 (Q4) should be the primary external source; Levels.fyi used as a high-resolution sanity check after normalizing for stock-value differences. Add a short sentence on how we adjust for stock-heavy offers.

2) Pay mix / total cash: add a small table showing recommended target % base vs target total cash by level (IC2/IC3/IC4/Manager/Director). This will avoid ad-hoc offers that look competitive on base but undershoot on OTE.

3) Remote hires and international policy: propose a cap of +20% uplift for APAC markets relative to US reference for hiring that uses a localized anchor (helps control offers in Singapore/Bangalore where demand skew can push comps up). For EU markets, use a 0–10% delta band depending on country-tier.

4) Governance: add a step — Compensation Committee pre-approval required for any offer >15% above the anchor. Also require Legal review for any non-standard equity structures (equity language varies across markets).

Minor: In the geo_anchor_model_v2.xlsx the Brazil multiplier looks optimistic; please include n for sample size in that tab.

No blocker — I can take the Pay Mix table and propose numbers by tomorrow 10am PT.

-Neha
Director, Total Rewards
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Dunne <adunne@skylark.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft: Compensation scale decision criteria and geo indexing + offer guardrails

Hi Marissa — appreciate the draft and the clarity. A couple of practical Qs from the ATS / recruiter side as we prepare candidate comps: 

1) For remote candidates who live in a different timezone but are willing to relocate later, do you treat them as local-market or US-reference market for the initial offer? Your note about "primary work location multiplier" — can you confirm whether that means the location on their passport / current residence or the location they agree to work from 6 months post-start?

2) Is there an internal field in Greenhouse you want populated to reflect the anchor multiplier used so hiring managers see the rationale in the offer packet? We can add a read-only field called "Comp Anchor (pct)" but need confirmation on expected values: e.g., 100% / 85% / 120%.

We are prepping candidate_comp_table.csv (sample attached) to demo how the multipliers will flow into offers and the approval thresholds. Happy to walk through tomorrow.

Best,
Alex Dunne
Senior Talent Partner
Skylark Inc. (Mercury Talent partner)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Compensation scale decision criteria and geo indexing + offer guardrails

Thanks everyone — consolidated decisions below so Talent and Recruiting have a single source of truth for execution. If there are objections, flag before EOD Thu 2027-06-10; otherwise Talent Ops to roll the updated language into the Offer Templates and Recruiting to push the Greenhouse changes.

Final decisions (approved):
- US reference percentiles by band: IC4/Staff = 60th, IC3/Senior = 55th, Manager = 55th, Director = 50th.
- Geo multipliers (reference = 100% US anchor): EU core markets = 95–105% (country-tier buckets to be documented), APAC core markets = 80–100% (Singapore capped at +15%), APAC emerging markets = 60–85% (Bangalore cap +20% only with People Ops signoff). LATAM markets = 70–90% with Brazil flagged for data quality checks.
- Remote hires: default to candidate's primary work location as captured in HR onboarding. Exceptions (candidate later relocates) will not trigger retroactive pay changes; exceptions during offer stage require manager + People Ops signoff.
- Approval gates: any offer >15% above the computed anchor requires Compensation Committee pre-approval; offers >25% above anchor require CFO notification.
- Pay mix: base target bands will be published in the Pay Mix table; Neha to deliver numbers for IC/Manager/Director by Fri 2027-06-11 10:00 PT.

Action items:
- Marissa: publish final comp language and upload revised attachments to the Drive (please include n/sample sizes in every market tab) — due Fri 2027-06-11 12:00 PT.
- Neha: provide Pay Mix table and run quick sanity check against FY26 offer history — due Fri 2027-06-11 10:00 PT.
- Recruiting (Alex/Skylark): add "Comp Anchor (pct)" read-only field in Greenhouse and demo flow — target Mon 2027-06-14.

Attachments updated: geo_anchor_model_v2.xlsx (v2.1 with sample-size column added), comp_scale_principles.docx (final language draft). Candidate_comp_table.csv used as demo only.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference
